unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision drops the sentence in which his mind refuses to imagine itself at rest or in a straight line. It now jumps from the dictionary definition straight to 'Since the question concerned the mind'. It also cuts 'One class of minds responded only to habit; another only to novelty. Race classified thought', which made 'unequally inert' concrete and led into race-inertia.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The redefinition as movement round habitual motives survives, as does the 'deceitful mistress' epigram.

evidence.quote: Finding that his mind refused to imagine itself at rest or in a straight line, he was forced, as usual, to let it imagine something else
His mind refused to imagine itself at rest or in a straight line, so he was forced, as usual, to let it imagine something else.
Since the question concerned the mind, and not matter, he decided from personal experience that his mind was never at rest
One class of minds responded only to habit; another only to novelty. Race classified thought.
had gone on complaining that minds were unequally inert. No two men thought alike, and no woman thought like a man.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's 'His mind refused... imagine something else' sentence and the two-sentence habit/novelty/race line.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: required (essential: redefinition of mental inertia; minds unequally inert)
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The self-mocking reason for abandoning the physical definition disappears, so the move into mental inertia reads as arbitrary. The contrast that seeds the race argument is also lost.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Inertia redefinition loses its comic hinge and the habit/novelty contrast

unresolved_should_improve.claim: Two sentences are dropped: the doubt whether race-inertia was ever overcome without destroying the race, and the claim that deflecting the American woman 'had interest infinitely greater' than any race. Paragraph 13 now ends on Americans ignoring sex, and 'surely' loses its comparative base.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: Paragraph 19's 'two large questions of vital importance to America' partially restates the stakes.

evidence.quote: History looked doubtful when asked whether race-inertia had ever been overcome without destroying the race in order to reconstruct it
Yet the task of accelerating or deflecting the movement of the American woman had interest infinitely greater than that of any race whatever
Race-inertia seemed to be fairly constant, and made the chief trouble in the Russian future; but surely sex-inertia had never been overcome at all.
The American always ostentatiously ignored sex, and American history mentioned hardly the name of a woman.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the 'History looked doubtful...' clause and the first draft's closing 'Yet the task... Asiatic or African' sentence.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: required (essential: race-inertia constant; sex-inertia never overcome; ending comparison)
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The chapter's final weighing ('Russia... somewhat easier... than the American') loses its setup. The reader is never told why the woman question outranks the Russian one.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Race-to-sex pivot and its stakes cut

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The first draft replaced Adams's wall image with the inserted phrase 'In that forecast'. The revision then cut the positions themselves: Russia's grasp, Cassini holding Hay, the Siberian checkmate, and Japan, England and Germany. 'These were the positions' now refers to a single sentence.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'seemed to him fixed' and 'the game seemed lost' still frame the outcome as Adams's 1903 view.

evidence.quote: Russia held Europe and America in her grasp, and Cassini held Hay in his. The Siberian Railway offered checkmate to all possible opposition.
The wall of Russian inertia that barred Europe across the Baltic, would bar America across the Pacific
Japan must make the best terms she could; England must go on receding; America and Germany would look on at the avalanche. In that forecast
and they seemed to him fixed. In that forecast, Hay's policy of the open door would infallibly fail.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore 'Russia held Europe and America in her grasp, and Cassini held Hay in his' and replace 'In that forecast' with the source's wall sentence.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: required (essential: insect's chart of spring 1903 as forecast)
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The 'map of political unity' and its checkmate imagery vanish. The forecast is asserted through non-authorial wording, and the Baltic/Pacific wall that bridges to the ice-cap is lost.
unresolved_should_improve.title: The insect's chart is emptied and replaced by an editorial phrase

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts the 'game--not the stakes' sentence. It also cuts 'To him even the extinction of the human race should be merely a fact to be grouped with other vital statistics.' The first draft kept both.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The census and Senate proposals and the 'Faust was helpless' line survive.

evidence.quote: for himself, the game--not the stakes--was the chief interest
To the humble student, the loss of Hay's game affected only Hay; for himself, the game--not the stakes--was the chief interest.
Thus the game seemed lost, in spite of the Kaiser's brilliant stroke. The Atlantic would have to deal with a vast continental mass
To him even the extinction of the human race should be merely a fact to be grouped with other vital statistics.
No honest historian can take part with--or against--the forces he has to study. The truth lay somewhere unconscious in the woman's breast.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore both sentences as they appear in the first draft.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: required (voice profile; essential: historian cannot take sides)
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: These are the chapter's signature acts of mock-scientific detachment, the historian treating Hay's ruin and humanity's end as data. Without them, the self-mockery and the statistical irony behind the census and Senate proposals are much thinner.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Narrator's impersonal detachment cut at two key points

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The sentence that Washington society 'was uneasy enough to need no further fretting' is cut. The ending now passes from 'gazed mute' directly to 'almost glad'.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: V7 and the 'nothing ever changed' irony are intact.

evidence.quote: but even in Washington, society was uneasy enough to need no further fretting. One was almost glad
Even in Washington, with its simple-minded standards of the field and farm, society was uneasy enough to need no further fretting.
One gazed mute before this ocean of darkest ignorance that had already engulfed society. One was almost glad to act the part of horseshoe crab

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's Washington sentence before 'One was almost glad'.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The crab's retreat into uniformity was a choice not to fret an already uneasy society. Without that sentence, the 'almost glad' irony is less grounded.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Horseshoe-crab retreat loses its motive

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The first draft dropped the historian's speculation that man overthrew the Church because it was feminine, so 'the overthrow of the Church' now has no agent. The revision also dropped 'although she secretly regretted the discard, she knew that she could not go backward'. As a result, 'marry machinery' follows an unqualified list.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'The historian... felt sometimes convinced' preserves some attribution.

evidence.quote: At times, the historian would have been almost willing to maintain that the man had overthrown the Church chiefly because it was feminine.
Although she secretly regretted the discard, she knew that she could not go backward.
She was free; she had no illusions; she was sexless; she had discarded all that the male disliked. She must, like the man, marry machinery.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the regret sentence and the 'At times, the historian...' speculation.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: required (essential: Church as woman's protest; marry machinery)
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: Adams's ambivalence becomes flat assertion: the woman's regret and irreversibility are lost. The causal link between man, Church and refuge is also lost, which bears on the plan's risk note about keeping period views as Adams's.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Woman's secret regret and the Church's overthrow lost
